sentences.text: In a study of humans, participants were asked to recall, suppress, or simply look at cues associated with unpleasant memories while their brain activity was measured using electroencephalography (EEG), a technique that records electrical signals from the scalp.
The results indicated that people with insomnia exhibited weaker memory control, as they forgot less of the memories they were instructed to suppress compared to the healthy group.

During the suppression phase, the insomnia group displayed higher P300 brain signals, a known marker of conscious memory retrieval, suggesting they continued to unconsciously retrieve the memories even when attempting to suppress them.
In contrast, the healthy group did not show this difference in brain signals, which suggests they successfully blocked the memory traces.
The authors conclude that future studies are needed to determine if these memory control deficits cause insomnia symptoms or are merely associated with them.
